newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ yields end higher as currency weakens further.
newsitem.headline: NZ yields end higher as currency weakens further.

* NZ yields rise in response to currency weakness
* Lingering bid tone seen in long bonds
* Retail sales slightly lower than forecast
New Zealand yields closed higher on Friday in response to a weaker currency but the dollar's late partial rebound arrested the slide.
Dealers said selling was not aggressive but turnover was steady.
Weakness in the U.S. market and softness in the U.S. treasuries set the tone for the bond market in the morning.

However, the 1.1 percent fall in November retail sales was a better number than economists had forecast and while little weight is attatched to one month's figures, dealers said it was more evidence of the economy slowing.
One dealer said there was a lingering bid tone in the bonds and others said there were plenty of buyers lurking in the 10-year bonds at 7.30 percent.

A slow start to next week is expected on Monday with Auckland and Australia out on holiday. However, September quarter current account figures will be watched with interest for any sign that the deficit was getting to a worrying size.
Economists forecast a $1.7 billion deficit for the quarter and $3.7 billion for the year.

Dealers said speads vs the U.S. had narrowed recently but they expect local assets to continue to outperform. -------------------------(SPREADS)------------------------------ Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close NZD VS 3 YR 10 YR * NZD 3-YR/10-YR SPREAD
